args.author: agent:xenobot
args.body: the document now says what the subject IS: a construct made from Xenopus laevis, inheriting 3 things and explicitly not inheriting 5. base.taxon still carries the DONOR, because the cells really are that taxon and the genome is unedited, so sequence questions stay answerable; everything organismal does not, and the tools that cannot tell the difference now refuse instead of answering about a frog.

made_from.what: a ciliated spheroid of donor skin and heart cells, 0.5-1 mm across, in a shape the donor never makes
made_from.source: DESIGN INPUT: what this construct IS, stated by the designer. Nothing in the ontologies describes it, because it is not anatomy.
inherits: whatever those cells do on their own
does_not_inherit: a gut, a mouth or gonads
a life cycle or a growth track
the donor range, community or predators

detail.caveat: This document describes a CONSTRUCT: an assembly made FROM a taxon, which is not an instance of that taxon. The distinction is the whole point of the field. A xenobot is built from Xenopus laevis cells and is not a frog: it has no organ systems, no gut, no gonads and a working life of days, and the donor's anatomy, life history, ecology and predators are facts about the donor and not about it. base.taxon still carries the DONOR, because the cells really are that taxon and the genome really is unedited, so genotype questions are answerable; everything organismal is not. Any tool that reads a taxon from this document must say which of the two it is answering about, and the ones that cannot tell the difference refuse.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
